title: La Fe's video course 'Watercolor Roses'
subtitle: Form, softness and living color in expressive florals

lessons.title: List of materials and photo reference
lessons.html_body:
Materials La Fe uses for the single-colored rose. He paints without a pencil sketch — the form is built in color. Lesson 1 shows his table; lesson 3 shows how he prepares the paper.

  1. Paper. Cotton watercolor paper, taped to a board. La Fe spends a full video on stretching and preparing the sheet — follow that rather than improvising.
  2. Paints. A small set of watercolors. He lets each hue do its own work instead of mixing everything on the palette. The overview video shows the exact colors for this rose.
  3. Brushes. Several rounds in different sizes and a wide flat / hake brush for wetting the sheet.
  4. Palette. A large white mixing tray.
  5. Water. Two jars — one for clean water, one for rinsing — plus a cloth or paper towel.
  6. Tape to hold the paper to the board.
  7. No pencil. La Fe does not draw the rose first. White paper left untouched is part of the painting.
  8. A live rose (or a clear photo) in front of you while you paint.

lessons.title: Analysis of the flower, arrangement, beginning of drawing
The secrets of using colors, working under a rosebud
List of materials and photo reference
lessons.html_body:
Materials La Fe uses for the two-colored rose. The setup is the same as the first lesson: no pencil, prepared paper, and a live flower in front of him.

  1. Paper. Cotton watercolor paper, taped to a board. Repeat the paper preparation from the first rose if you are starting here.
  2. Paints. A small set of watercolors, with more contrast between the two hues of the petals plus greens for the leaves. The overview video shows the exact colors for this rose.
  3. Brushes. Several rounds in different sizes and a wide flat / hake brush for wetting the sheet.
  4. Palette. A large white mixing tray.
  5. Water. Two jars — one for clean water, one for rinsing — plus a cloth or paper towel.
  6. Tape to hold the paper to the board.
  7. No pencil. La Fe builds the two-colored rose in paint only. Untouched paper is the light.
  8. A live rose (or a clear photo) in front of you while you paint.

Photo reference

The two-colored rose on La Fe’s table in this lesson — the live flower and the painting in progress.
